craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as will-born glory; bhakti as pratyabhijñā; vyabhicāri wonder (camatkāra) at one-yet-many. Sanskrit-first: sahaja/bhrānti opens kept (natural/delusion held per UNC); ekopy anekātmakam (ONE yet MANY-SELFed — non-cancelling kept, never resolved); You-capital kept (address IS the Lord). Abhinavagupta frame: ābhāsa shining-by-beholding (no arising needed — being-beheld suffices); will (icchā) as the sole birth. Rows: 9 (one/many pair — kept paired; resolving would cancel the verse), 7 (You addressed mid-verse — beholding MADE second-person), 1 (‘many-selfed’ closes — multiplicity last, uncancelled). Close: ‘one and yet many-selfed’. Rupture: ‘so in splendor’ (cosmogony turns to shining — birth-account becomes praise). Rejected: resolving one-yet-many — killed: non-cancelling IS the verse; lowercasing you — killed: address is the Lord; ‘through your gaze’ for beholding — killed: darśana-beholding kept plain. Read aloud: THINGS do NOT a-RISE … EVEN the un-TRUE par-TAKES of TRUTH … THIS-glo-ry OF-worlds is WILL-born OF-you … ONE and YET man-y-SELFED.

lines: Things do not arise; by nature they shine through your beholding — even the untrue partakes of truth for a moment, through experience’s delusion.
This glory of worlds is will-born of You, with birth from nowhere else — so in splendor You shine through the worlds, one and yet many-selfed.

reads_against.argmap: Do things arise, and whence the universe-glory? → No arising; things shine by contemplation; non-true borrows momentary truth; universe-glory is will-born; you shine one-yet-many.
c1_essence: Of things no arising; naturally they shine by your contemplation, even the non-true borrowing momentary truth. This universe-glory is will-born from you, birth from elsewhere denied; hence you shine in worlds — one, yet many-selfed. Nonduality without cancelling multiplicity: one, yet many-selfed.
